Theme

consolation noun

also comfort (noun), solace, relief

classical

Plaut. Amph. 643: id sōlāciō est
Cic. Tusc. 2.59: haec sunt sōlācia, haec fōmenta summōrum dolōrum (Lewis & Short)

sōlācium, sōlāciī n.

noun, second declension

a comfort, a solace, something that eases grief

Sōlāciō esse (dative), to be a comfort to someone.

Other words

  • cōnsōlātiō, cōnsōlātiōnis f. — the act of consoling; words of comfort

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Cic. Tusc. 3.77: nōn egēre cōnsōlātiōne (Lewis & Short); Cic. Fam. 5.13.1: litterārum tuārum (Lewis & Short)

Examples

  • haec sunt sōlācia, haec fōmenta summōrum dolōrum

    these are the comforts, these the poultices for the greatest painsCic. Tusc. 2.59 (Lewis & Short)

See also comfort, grieve, grief.

SourcesLewis & Short: solacium · Lewis & Short: consolatio

Plautus, Amphitruo 643.
